text:
Ravi: Hey all, first-week laptop snag. Enrolled my MacBook Air (macOS 13.6.4) but I keep getting a login window asking for an 'Institutional Recovery Key' on wake and FileVault says 'Unable to enable'. Also I don't have admin rights to install Homebrew so blocked for dev setup. Anyone run into this?

Sam (IT): Welcome! That recovery key prompt usually shows if FileVault was partially enabled then aborted. Can you paste `fdesetup status` and confirm if the device is supervised? If you can't install Homebrew, we can grant a short-lived admin token.

Ravi: fdesetup output: "FileVault is Off. No user is enabled for FileVault." Device Bot shows supervised: yes. I did enroll via the Okta SSO flow so no local admin.

Priya (Buddy): @Ravi hey! I ran into this last month. IT pushed an MDM command to finish FV enable with the org key and it cleared up. You might need to accept a prompt to allow the MDM to proceed.

Sam (IT): Since device is supervised we can enable FileVault with institutional escrow. I'll push the command now. You should see a modal: "Redwood Device Management requests to enable FileVault using the organization recovery key". Click Accept and enter your password when prompted.

MDM Bot: Pushing FileVault enable (institutional escrow) for device id a9b3f1. Expect user confirmation and reboot.

Ravi: Got the modal, accepted and entered password. It showed "Enabling FileVault..." then asked for a reboot. Rebooted.

Ravi: Post-reboot checks: `fdesetup status` -> "FileVault is On. Users enabled for FileVault: - ravi". System Settings shows FileVault: On. Also Sam, can I get the temporary admin window for Homebrew?

Sam (IT): Granting a 4-hour sudo window for user ravi. Please run the installer and reply when done so I can revoke.

Ravi: Installed Homebrew and docker, all good. Thanks everyone!

Sam (IT): Closing: Enabled FV via institutional escrow and issued temporary admin for dev setup. If others hit this, supervised devices can use the escrow flow to avoid sharing creds."
